key_insight: This paper extends 3D Gaussian Splatting from static scenes to scenes with flowing water, making high-quality novel view synthesis more realistic in dynamic environments. The core idea is to model water-like motion in a way that remains practical under casual capture conditions.
problem_solved: Standard 3D Gaussian Splatting works well for static scenes but struggles with high-frequency dynamic effects like water flow. The paper addresses the challenge of reconstructing and animating realistic water without requiring dense multi-view or high-speed capture setups.
method: Builds on explicit 3D Gaussian Splatting scene representations to handle dynamic water behavior.
Introduces a motion-aware modeling approach designed for complex, high-frequency fluid motion.
Targets casual capture settings, aiming to preserve visual realism while keeping reconstruction practical and efficient.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this expands the applicability of 3DGS to a broader class of real-world scenes with dynamic fluid effects. It is especially relevant for robotics, AR/VR, digital twins, and content creation where realistic water motion improves scene fidelity.

paper_title: Make It Flow: Animating Water in 3D Gaussian Splatting Scenes
paper_authors: Kjell Keune, Florian Hahlbohm, Jannis Möller, Susana Castillo, Martin Eisemann
